explanation: The siege article says where the garrison went: "the defending French garrison under Jean-Pierre Marie Lavalette du Verdier evacuated the city and retreated to Cap-Français." The Vertières article says what was left a fortnight later: "The only places controlled by the French forces were Môle St. Nicolas, held by Noailles, and Cap-Français, where, with 5,000 troops, French General Rochambeau was at bay." Precondition and not cause: two articles say the fall of the capital concentrated the French where the last battle was fought; neither says it decided it. Probable: Wikipedia alone.
